topic: Theme F: Religion, Human Rights & Social Justice

items.title: Kant gave multiple formulations of the categorical imperative
items.claim: How does Kant's categorical imperative work?

options.text: A single rule: do unto others as you would have them do to you

Multiple formulations including universalisability ('act only according to that maxim by which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law') and humanity-as-end ('act so as to treat humanity, in your own person or another's, always as an end, never as a means only')
An empirical rule derived from observation

items.reveal:
Kant's 'Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals' (1785) sets out the categorical imperative. Standard count: three formulations.

Formula of Universal Law: 'Act only according to that maxim by which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.'
Formula of Humanity: 'Act so as to treat humanity... always as an end, never as a means only.'
Formula of the Kingdom of Ends: 'Act according to the maxims of a member of a merely possible kingdom of ends.'

Kant's most famous example — lying to the murderer at the door — shows the strict reading: lying is universally impermissible.
items.why: Kantian ethics is sometimes reduced to 'don't lie'. The multiple formulations and the humanity-as-end principle are richer — and more humane — than the slogan suggests.

items.title: Ramadan moves through the year on the lunar calendar
items.claim: Why does Ramadan fall in different seasons across years?

options.text: It is fixed each year by Islamic council

The Islamic (Hijri) calendar is purely lunar with no intercalation; its 12 months total around 354 days; Ramadan therefore shifts about 11 days earlier each Gregorian year, cycling through all seasons over around 33 years
It is fixed to August every year

items.reveal:
Most other religious calendars (Jewish, Hindu, Buddhist) are lunisolar — they add intercalary months to keep festivals in fixed seasons. The Islamic calendar deliberately rejects intercalation, based on Quran 9:36-37.

The Hijri year begins from Muhammad's emigration (hijra) from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE. The Hijri year 1446 began in July 2024.

In tropical countries Ramadan stays around 12-14 hours of fasting daylight; in high latitudes in summer it can exceed 20 hours, raising practical questions for which contemporary scholars give differing rulings.
items.why: Calendar choices have theological consequences. The Islamic refusal to align the lunar year with the seasons produces a religious experience that cycles through climates and seasons — different from Christianity or Judaism.

items.title: Ten human Sikh Gurus, then the eternal Guru Granth Sahib
items.claim: How does the Sikh tradition handle leadership after Guru Gobind Singh?

options.text: It ended with the tenth Guru with no continuation
In 1708 Guru Gobind Singh declared the Guru Granth Sahib (the scripture) to be the eternal Guru — no further human gurus
It continues through a hereditary line

items.reveal:
Guru Gobind Singh died in 1708 from a stab wound inflicted by an Afghan assassin. Before his death he installed the Adi Granth (compiled by Guru Arjan in 1604) as Guru Granth Sahib — making the scripture the eternal Guru.

The Guru Granth Sahib (1,430 pages, mostly in Gurmukhi script) contains hymns by six of the ten Gurus, plus 15 Hindu and Muslim saints (bhagats) — including Kabir and Sheikh Farid. It is treated as a living Guru: bowed to, awakened in the morning, put to rest at night.

Sikh gurdwaras place the Guru Granth Sahib on a throne (palki) as the central focus.
items.why: The structural innovation of designating scripture as eternal Guru ended succession disputes that plague many religions. Sikh community continuity rests on the text, not on a living hierarchy.
